name: Seoraksan and Sokcho
tagline: Jagged granite peaks, waterfalls, hermitages and autumn colour beside a sea-view fishing port known for squid and sundae.
highlight: A cable car to Gwongeumseong fortress, with the granite spires of Seoraksan spread out below in October.
shortDescription: South Korea's most beautiful mountain park, with the Ulsanbawi rock, Biryong Falls, the cable car to Gwongeumseong and hiking to Daecheongbong, plus the port town of Sokcho and its seafood market.
metaDescription: A Seoraksan and Sokcho travel guide: Ulsanbawi, Gwongeumseong cable car, Biryong Falls, Sinheungsa temple, Daecheongbong hike, autumn colour, Sokcho seafood, where to stay and a two-day plan.

image.alt: A wide panorama of the granite peaks of Seoraksan National Park

intro: Seoraksan is the crown of the Taebaek range in Gangwon Province, and South Korea's most beloved mountain park. Its highest peak, Daecheongbong, reaches 1,708 metres, the third highest in the country, and its landscape is one of sharp granite ridges, deep valleys, waterfalls and old pines. It is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, and it is the country's most reliable place to see autumn foliage, which usually peaks in the second half of October.

The park is easy to enjoy at any level. Short walks lead from the entrance to Sinheungsa Temple and a giant bronze Buddha, cable cars go up to the ruined fortress of Gwongeumseong for wide views, and longer trails climb to Ulsanbawi, a rock face reached by steep stairs, and Biryong Falls. Experienced hikers can cross to Daecheongbong on a long day, often with an overnight stay in a mountain shelter.

The gateway is Sokcho, a small port town on the coast, where fishing boats unload squid, and where you can eat sundae (blood sausage) and fresh raw fish at Sokcho Tourist Fish Market. It is about two and a half hours from Seoul by express bus, and the sea and mountains are so close that you can watch a sunrise on the beach and hike in the afternoon.

attractions.name: Gwongeumseong and the cable car

image.alt: A footbridge crossing a valley at Seoraksan National Park

attractions.text: A cable car rises to a mountain fortress with sweeping views over the peaks, followed by a short climb.
attractions.tip: Book early in October, since queues can be long.

attractions.name: Ulsanbawi Rock
attractions.text: A huge rock formation reached by a hike of about 3.8 km and 800 steps, with big views.
attractions.tip: Start early, and expect a steep climb.

attractions.name: Biryong Falls
attractions.text: A waterfall reached by an easy trail through a forest.

attractions.name: Sinheungsa Temple
attractions.text: A temple founded in the 7th century at the park's entrance, with a giant bronze Buddha.

attractions.name: Sokcho Tourist Fish Market
attractions.text: A market of seafood stalls and restaurants, with fresh squid and crab.

attractions.name: Abai Village
attractions.text: A village of North Korean refugees on a small strip of land, reached by a hand-pulled ferry, known for its squid sundae.

bestTime.headline: October for colour
bestTime.summary: Seoraksan is cold in winter and pleasant in spring and autumn.

seasons.text: Cool on the mountain, with rain.
Peak foliage in mid to late October.
Snow and ice, with limited trails.

bestTime.avoid: Weekends in peak foliage, and winter without equipment.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you hike Seoraksan.
tips: Go on a weekday in October.
Book buses and rooms early in autumn.

faq.q: When is Seoraksan at its best?
faq.a: The second half of October, for autumn colour.

faq.q: How do I get there from Seoul?
faq.a: An express bus to Sokcho, then a local bus to the park.

faq.q: Do I need to be fit?
faq.a: Not for the short walks. Ulsanbawi and Daecheongbong are strenuous.

faq.q: Is it worth going in winter?
faq.a: Yes for snow scenery, with care.

faq.q: Can I combine it with Gangneung?
faq.a: Yes, they are about an hour apart.
